title: A Workshop on Observation
paragraphs: The writing workshop began with an unusual assignment: compare several brief records before composing a conclusion. Each record offered a glimpse of a different situation. The participants had to respect those differences while discovering a theme that could give their discussion a clear direction.

The opening pages introduced several situations worth examining carefully. A peculiar smell unlike anything familiar drifted from the cupboard. Include only evidence relevant to the question being discussed. The injured runner made a remarkable recovery that surprised everyone. The new bridge made a significant difference to travel times.

The remaining pages widened the discussion with additional observations. A superficial inspection missed the serious damage beneath the surface. The superior design proved stronger and easier to use than the alternatives. Do not let a trivial disagreement ruin an important friendship. The conclusion is valid because the evidence supports it.

By the end of the discussion, the students had learned why careful reading requires more than a quick judgment. A useful interpretation must fit the details of the situation. They chose a conclusion that acknowledged differences among the accounts, and they left readers with a question: which observation most strongly supports your view, and what might change your mind?

targets.definition: closely connected to the matter at hand
important enough to have an effect
supported by sound reasoning or evidence
